standingLimitations: Marsden Farm is one research site over nine seasons. Nothing here predicts what will happen on this field.
Climate indicators are POWER grid values, about 50 km across, not field measurements.
Soil values come from a mapped survey, not from sampling this field.
Every applicability rule is a team-proposed guardrail and is not expert-reviewed.
No profitability is calculated; the data PRD 9 requires for it is not available.

strategies.label: Existing system
operational_requirements: Equipment and markets already in place for maize and soybean

strategies.label: Diversified option
operational_requirements: A use or buyer for oat grain and straw
Red clover establishment, usually frost-seeded into the small grain
Manure access: the Marsden three-year system received composted manure
Equipment and labour for small-grain harvest

strategies.label: Diversified option
operational_requirements: A forage use or buyer for alfalfa across two years of the rotation
Alfalfa establishment, multiple cuts per season, and storage or handling for forage
Manure access: the Marsden four-year system received composted manure
Equipment and labour for small-grain and forage harvest
Commitment to keep a quarter of the land out of maize and soybean for two years at a time

outcomes.label: Lower applied nitrogen (manufactured plus manure)
outcomes.source: Davis et al. (2012) supplementary management records [S10]; reproduced in AgroCycle reproduction, transform/marsden (roadmap Phase 6)
outcomes.statement: In the Marsden experiment, nine-year applied N averaged 74.5, 56.6 and 40.8 kg N/ha/yr for the two-, three- and four-year systems, and manufactured N alone was 74.5, 16.7 and 10.9. These are rotation-area-weighted averages from one site over nine seasons.
outcomes.caution: These figures come from one research farm over nine seasons, so they are not a prediction for your field. The diversified systems also received manure, so this is not a drop in the nitrogen the crop received, and it leaves out the nitrogen the clover and alfalfa fix themselves.

outcomes.label: Lower herbicide active ingredient per hectare per year
outcomes.source: Davis et al. (2012) supplementary management records [S10]; reproduced in AgroCycle reproduction, transform/marsden (roadmap Phase 6)
outcomes.statement: In the Marsden experiment, herbicide active ingredient averaged 1.925, 0.261 and 0.195 kg ai/ha/yr for the two-, three- and four-year systems, about 86-90 % lower in the diversified systems.
outcomes.caution: This is the weight of herbicide applied, which says nothing about how harmful it is or who was exposed to it. Insecticides used in 2007 to 2009 are not counted. One research farm over nine seasons is not a prediction for your field.

outcomes.label: Maize and soybean yields matched or exceeded the two-year system
outcomes.source: Davis et al. (2012), PLOS ONE 7(10): e47149 [S09]
outcomes.statement: The publication reports that maize and soybean yields in the diversified systems matched or exceeded the two-year system. This is attributed to the paper.
outcomes.caution: This is the researchers' own published result. We have not recalculated it, because the data they published does not include the field-by-field yields. It does not predict what your field would yield.

outcomes.label: No significant difference in net returns between systems
outcomes.source: Davis et al. (2012), PLOS ONE 7(10): e47149 [S09]
outcomes.statement: The publication reports no significant difference in net returns between the systems, under its own price and cost assumptions.
outcomes.caution: This was true at their prices and costs, on their farm. AgroCycle does not work out profit: that would need your yields, input costs, machinery, labour, transport and prices, and we have none of them.
outcomes.caution_reference: Davis et al. (2012); AgroCycle scope (PRD section 9)

outcomes.label: Weed suppression in the diversified systems
outcomes.source: Davis et al. (2012), PLOS ONE 7(10): e47149 [S09]
outcomes.statement: The publication reports its own weed findings, which are attributed to it and not recomputed.
outcomes.caution: The records we reproduced cover herbicide applied, not weed numbers. The weed findings are the researchers' own and do not predict weed pressure on your field.

outcomes.label: Soil carbon gain
outcomes.caution: Nothing AgroCycle uses measures soil carbon on a field, and the experiment's records do not show a soil-carbon gain. Shown as not assessed.

outcomes.label: Measured erosion reduction
outcomes.caution: Nothing AgroCycle uses measures erosion on a field. Estimating it would need a method the team has not agreed, so it is shown as not assessed.

outcomes.label: Measured nitrate-leaching reduction
outcomes.caution: Applying less nitrogen is not the same as measuring less nitrate leaving the soil. Nothing AgroCycle uses measures leaching, so it is shown as not assessed.

outcomes.label: Forage produced for on-farm use or sale
outcomes.caution: We have no figures for forage yield, quality or feed value: no source found yet. That the four-year rotation grows alfalfa for two years is part of how the rotation is defined, not a measured amount of feed.

rules.condition_text: The farmer has no access to manure.
rules.rationale: Manure supplied 39.9 and 29.9 kg N/ha/yr of the three- and four-year systems' applied nitrogen. Without manure the diversified systems as tested at Marsden cannot be reproduced, so the applied nitrogen comparison does not transfer.

rules.condition_text: Manure access has not been stated.
rules.rationale: Missing data is not evidence of access (PRD 8.5). The outcome is withheld until the farmer says, rather than assumed either way.

rules.condition_text: The field's recent crop history is not a maize-soybean rotation.
rules.rationale: Every Marsden comparison is measured against a two-year maize-soybean baseline. A field in continuous maize, pasture or a non-rotation sequence is outside the experiment's domain, so the comparison is not offered for it.

rules.condition_text: Crop history could not be classified.
rules.rationale: A field whose CDL history is unavailable or low-confidence cannot be placed in or out of the domain, so the engine abstains rather than assuming the baseline.

rules.condition_text: The field lies outside Story or Boone County, Iowa.
rules.rationale: The MVP's soil, climate and validation resources were assembled for these two counties (PRD 2.3). A field elsewhere is not excluded, but the comparison is qualified because the supporting context was not assembled for it.

rules.condition_text: The field's growing-season GDD differs from the Marsden site by more than 300 degree-days C.
rules.rationale: A field with a materially different heat accumulation may not support the same crop sequence. The band is deliberately wide and the effect is a qualification, not exclusion, because no published basis for a threshold was available. This is the weakest rule in the table.

rules.condition_text: The climate comparison with the Marsden site could not be computed.
rules.rationale: An unknown climate distance is not a close one. The comparison may still be shown, qualified, with the gap named.

rules.condition_text: The field's dominant SSURGO drainage class is poorly or very poorly drained.
rules.rationale: Depends on crop claim alfalfa_drainage_sensitivity, which is research_needed. The rule is recorded so the question is visible and reviewable; if no source is found it must be withdrawn rather than applied. SSURGO also does not record installed tile drainage, which could change the answer for a given field.

rules.condition_text: The field's frost-free window is shorter than 120 days.
rules.rationale: Depends on crop claim oat_season_window, which is research_needed. Recorded for review; withdraw if unsourced. The frost-free figure is a POWER grid value, not a field measurement.

rules.condition_text: There is no on-farm forage use and no buyer for alfalfa.
rules.rationale: The four-year rotation grows alfalfa for two years of four. With no use and no buyer the rotation is not operationally available, whatever the environmental evidence says (PRD 9).

rules.condition_text: There is no on-farm use and no buyer for oat grain or straw.
rules.rationale: A single small-grain phase with no outlet is a real feasibility problem but a smaller commitment than two years of alfalfa, so it qualifies the option rather than removing it (PRD 9).

rules.condition_text: Neither small-grain equipment nor a contractor is available.
rules.rationale: Equipment and labour for small-grain harvest are an operational requirement of both diversified options and a first-class constraint, not explanatory text (PRD 9).

rules.condition_text: Whether there is a forage use or buyer has not been stated.
rules.rationale: An unstated outlet is not an available one. The option is shown with the question attached rather than treated as operationally settled (PRD 8.5).

rules.condition_text: Whether there is an oat use or buyer has not been stated.
rules.rationale: An unstated outlet is not an available one; the option is qualified until the farmer says (PRD 8.5).

rules.condition_text: Small-grain equipment or contractor access has not been stated.
rules.rationale: Unstated machinery access is not assumed access. Both diversified options need small-grain harvest, so the question is carried into the comparison (PRD 8.5, 9).

rules.condition_text: One or more required profile indicators came back unknown.
rules.rationale: PRD 8.5: missing data is never evidence of no risk or no benefit. An indicator that returned 'unknown' withholds the dimensions that depend on it instead of being read as neutral.
